summary: No new numbered sense is warranted. Funeral weeping remains weinen; the German rendering Klagelieder does not establish singing as a distinct Turoyo meaning. The dog speaker repairs koboxən to konawḥi; it cannot establish an independent canine crying sense.

The input entry ALREADY contains Nomen actionis examples at 60/96 and 77/75. Readers repeatedly overlooked that box while calling for Infinitiv. All baxyo event nouns, including possessed forms, belong to Nomen Actionis here; they are neither a new lexeme nor Detransitive.

New secure boxes are Infectum-wa (buxewo/boxewa/buxyowa), Part act. (baxoye/baxayto) and Imperativ (bxay). Preterit Intransitive baxi/baxyo may present an onset without a separate start verb. Infectum can narrate past crying vividly.
III makes the cause a subject and the crying participant a suffixed object or an omitted generic participant; inanimate letters/events occur as causes. Existing sense weinen machen covers these uses.
References prs 3/21 and supplied PrS 1/35 represent the same existing source quotation. Existing action-noun quotations at 60/96 and 77/75 are not re-added.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce English is project machine translation, not an edition translation. All semantic decisions rest on the supplied Turoyo; retained English quotations are verbatim machine translation. Only round-2 changes are encoded here.

Round 1 already has I Infectum-wa, Imperativ, Part act. and five Nomen Actionis examples. Repeated Infinitiv/new-form proposals in the Jan analysis do not create new boxes. All nominal baxyo/bəxoyo occurrences follow the inherited Nomen Actionis placement.
New boxes are III Infectum-wa, III Part act., and I Preterit-wa. Baxiwo in Jan 1.36/1514 contrasts with buxewo in 1513; tense/aspect placement rests on vowel and suffix shape, not English was crying.

The funeral-practice account makes a valency contrast explicit: I buxanwo has the crier as subject; III mabxanwole has the causee as an additional argument. A cognate nominal baxyo in 1.15/593 does not establish ordinary transitivity.
The plural -an- occurs in clauses about gawre as well as niše (Jan 1.15/590–591). Do not infer female agreement solely from this ending. The transcription also uses baxoye/mabxəyone for women.

summary: Jan funeral practice supports round 1’s treatment of lamenting as weinen rather than a new singing sense. Skilled baxoye/baxayto and cognate baxyo occur alongside ordinary weeping; a craft designation does not by itself change the verb meaning.
Customary lamenters cause other mourners to weep, with overt u ʕamo kule and suffix -le, or omitted causees. This extends round-1 letter/event causes and supports the existing causative sense.
